findings.title: SQL injection: search term concatenated directly into query text
findings.evidence: The query is built by concatenating the caller-supplied term into the SQL literal instead of binding it as a parameter: '    q = "SELECT * FROM docs WHERE title LIKE '%" + term + "%"''
findings.evidence_quote: q = "SELECT * FROM docs WHERE title LIKE '%" + term + "%'"
findings.recommendation: Revert to parameter binding: build the pattern in Python and pass it as a bound parameter, e.g. q = "SELECT * FROM docs WHERE title LIKE ?" and db.execute(q, (f"%{term}%",)). If the LIKE pattern must be escaped, escape % and _ in term before binding.

findings.title: Benign search terms with a quote break the query (no params bound)
findings.evidence: The statement is executed with no parameters, so a term such as "O'Brien" produces unbalanced quotes and the SQL layer raises an OperationalError instead of returning results: '    return db.execute(q)'
findings.recommendation: Bind the term as a parameter (db.execute(q, (f"%{term}%",))) so quoting is handled by the driver; add a regression test searching for a term containing a single quote and one containing % / _.
